events.name: Full-scale invasion begins
events.description: Russia invades from the north, east and south, with missile strikes on cities and military sites across Ukraine.

events.name: Battle of Hostomel Airport
events.description: Russian airborne troops assault Antonov Airport to open an air bridge to Kyiv; Ukrainian forces wreck the runway.

events.name: Siege of Mariupol
events.description: Russian forces encircle and level much of Mariupol; the last defenders in the Azovstal steelworks surrender in May.

events.name: Battle of Kyiv
events.description: Russian columns push on Kyiv through Irpin and Bucha but stall, and withdraw from the north by early April.

events.name: Bucha massacre
events.description: Over 400 bodies are found in Bucha after Russia's withdrawal; many civilians were tortured and executed.

events.name: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant seized
events.description: Russian troops shell and capture Europe's largest nuclear power plant, which they still occupy.

events.name: Mariupol theatre airstrike
events.description: An airstrike hits a theatre sheltering civilians and marked 'children' outside; Amnesty called it a war crime.

events.name: Kramatorsk station missile strike
events.description: A missile with cluster munitions hits a station crowded with evacuees, killing 61 civilians.

events.name: Sinking of the Moskva
events.description: Ukrainian Neptune missiles hit the flagship of Russia's Black Sea Fleet, which sinks the next day.

events.name: Battle of Sievierodonetsk-Lysychansk
events.description: Russia takes the last cities of Luhansk oblast after weeks of artillery-heavy fighting.

events.name: Battle of Bakhmut
events.description: The war's longest battle: Wagner and Russian forces take Bakhmut at great cost after months of fighting.

events.name: Kherson counteroffensive
events.description: Ukraine cuts Russian supply lines over the Dnipro, forcing Russia out of Kherson city and the west bank.

events.name: Kharkiv counteroffensive
events.description: A rapid Ukrainian offensive retakes Balakliia, Kupiansk and Izium, collapsing Russia's front in Kharkiv oblast.

events.name: Strikes on the power grid
events.description: Waves of Russian missiles and drones target Ukraine's power plants and grid, causing blackouts through winter.

events.name: 2023 Ukrainian counteroffensive
events.description: Ukraine's push south through Zaporizhzhia oblast meets dense minefields and gains little ground.

events.name: Kakhovka Dam destroyed
events.description: The dam's collapse floods towns along the lower Dnipro and drains its reservoir; it is widely blamed on Russia.

events.name: Battle of Avdiivka
events.description: Russia takes the heavily fortified town near Donetsk after a four-month assault, its first big gain since Bakhmut.

events.name: Okhmatdyt children's hospital strike
events.description: A Russian missile hits Ukraine's largest children's hospital in Kyiv during a mass strike on the city.

events.name: Kursk incursion
events.description: Ukraine invades Russia's Kursk region, taking Sudzha; Russia, aided by North Korean troops, retakes it by spring.

events.name: US-led invasion begins
events.description: US and British airstrikes open Operation Enduring Freedom against the Taliban and al-Qaeda after the 9/11 attacks.

events.name: Fall of Mazar-i-Sharif
events.description: Northern Alliance forces, aided by US special forces and airpower, take the north's largest city.

events.name: Fall of Kabul
events.description: The Taliban abandon Kabul and Northern Alliance forces enter the capital.

events.name: Fall of Kandahar
events.description: The Taliban surrender their spiritual capital, ending their rule; Mullah Omar escapes.

events.name: Battle of Tora Bora
events.description: US-backed Afghan militias assault al-Qaeda's mountain caves, but Osama bin Laden escapes into Pakistan.

events.name: Operation Anaconda
events.description: US and allied troops attack Taliban and al-Qaeda fighters in the Shah-i-Kot Valley in the war's first big battle.

events.name: Operation Medusa
events.description: Canadian-led NATO troops drive Taliban fighters from Panjwayi near Kandahar as the insurgency grows.

events.name: Battle of Marjah
events.description: The surge's first major offensive retakes the Taliban stronghold of Marjah in Helmand province.

events.name: Killing of Osama bin Laden
events.description: US Navy SEALs kill the al-Qaeda leader in a raid on his compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan.

events.name: Kandahar massacre
events.description: A US soldier kills 16 villagers, most of them women and children, in two villages in Panjwayi district.

events.name: End of NATO combat mission
events.description: ISAF hands security to Afghan forces and gives way to a smaller NATO training mission.

events.name: Taliban capture Kunduz
events.description: The Taliban seize Kunduz, their first provincial capital since 2001, before Afghan forces retake it.

events.name: Kunduz hospital airstrike
events.description: A US gunship repeatedly strikes a Doctors Without Borders hospital, killing 42 patients and staff.

events.name: MOAB strike in Achin
events.description: The US drops its largest non-nuclear bomb on an Islamic State tunnel complex in Nangarhar province.

events.name: Kabul truck bombing
events.description: A truck bomb in Kabul's diplomatic quarter kills more than 90 people and wounds hundreds.

events.name: Doha Agreement
events.description: The US and the Taliban agree on a full US troop withdrawal in exchange for Taliban security guarantees.

events.name: Kabul maternity ward attack
events.description: Gunmen attack a maternity ward in Dasht-e-Barchi, killing 24, including mothers and newborns.

events.name: 2021 Taliban offensive
events.description: As US troops withdraw, the Taliban take rural districts, then provincial capitals in quick succession.

events.name: Taliban take Kabul
events.description: President Ghani flees and the Taliban enter Kabul, retaking power after 20 years.

events.name: Kabul airport bombing
events.description: An Islamic State suicide bombing at the airport's Abbey Gate kills about 170 Afghans and 13 US troops.

events.name: Daraa protests
events.description: Protests over the arrest of boys for anti-Assad graffiti meet live fire, sparking a nationwide uprising.

events.name: Siege of Homs
events.description: Government forces besiege opposition districts of Homs for three years until rebels evacuate the old city.

events.name: Houla massacre
events.description: 108 villagers, nearly half of them children, are killed; UN investigators blamed pro-government forces.

events.name: Battle of Aleppo
events.description: Syria's largest city is split for four years until a siege and bombing campaign retakes its east for the government.

events.name: Ghouta chemical attack
events.description: Sarin rockets hit opposition-held Ghouta outside Damascus, killing hundreds; UN inspectors confirmed sarin use.

events.name: ISIS takes Raqqa
events.description: The Islamic State drives out other rebel groups and makes Raqqa the capital of its self-declared caliphate.

events.name: Siege of Kobani
events.description: Kurdish YPG fighters, backed by US-led airstrikes, hold Kobani against ISIS in a turning point against the group.

events.name: ISIS captures Palmyra
events.description: ISIS seizes Palmyra, carrying out mass executions and blowing up the ancient city's temples.

events.name: Russian intervention begins
events.description: Russian airstrikes from Hmeimim air base begin, turning the war in the government's favour.

events.name: Khan Shaykhun chemical attack
events.description: A sarin attack kills about 90 people; UN-OPCW investigators blamed the Syrian government, and the US strikes back.

events.name: Battle of Raqqa
events.description: The Kurdish-led SDF, backed by coalition airstrikes, takes Raqqa from ISIS, leaving much of the city destroyed.

events.name: Operation Olive Branch
events.description: Turkey and allied Syrian rebels take the Kurdish-held Afrin region, displacing much of its population.

events.name: Eastern Ghouta offensive
events.description: A month-long siege and bombardment retakes the last rebel enclave near Damascus, killing over 1,500 civilians.

events.name: Douma chemical attack
events.description: A chlorine attack kills dozens in Douma; the OPCW later attributed it to the Syrian air force.

events.name: Battle of Baghuz
events.description: The SDF takes Baghuz, the last village held by ISIS, ending its territorial caliphate.

events.name: Operation Peace Spring
events.description: After US troops pull back, Turkey invades the Kurdish-held northeast, taking Ras al-Ayn and Tal Abyad.

events.name: Northwest offensive
events.description: Government and Russian forces push into Idlib, displacing nearly a million people before a March ceasefire.

events.name: Opposition offensive on Aleppo
events.description: HTS-led rebels launch a surprise offensive from Idlib and take Aleppo within days, then sweep south.

events.name: Fall of the Assad government
events.description: Rebels enter Damascus as Bashar al-Assad flees to Russia, ending more than 50 years of his family's rule.
